_comment_rewrites: Without this file every route that is not prerendered was served dist/404.html
with a real HTTP 404 status. The page still rendered — React booted and drew the
right screen — so it looked like nothing more than a wrong tab title. It was not.
· /admin/students/<uuid>  — the whole admin, 404 to every monitor and crawler
That second one is the reason this matters. A certificate's QR is the school's
proof of itself. An employer scanning one got a 404 from the server before the
app ever loaded, and link previewers, corporate proxies and security scanners act
on the status code, not on what renders afterwards.
Vercel checks the filesystem BEFORE rewrites, so the 13 prerendered pages and
every hashed asset still win. Only genuinely unmatched paths fall through to the
app, which then routes them itself — including showing its own 404 screen.
_comment_headers: Asset filenames carry a content hash, so a changed file is a changed URL and the
old one can be cached forever. HTML must NOT be: a stale document pins the asset
hashes it was built with, and a visitor holding one after a deploy fetches chunks
that no longer exist — the blank screen that looks like the app is broken.
